niche: connected TV and streaming advertising agency
prompt_text: What is the best connected TV advertising agency?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” connected TV (CTV) advertising agency — the right one depends on your goals, budget, audience, measurement needs and whether you want a full-service agency, a programmatic partner, or direct access to platform inventory. Below I’ll summarize how to choose and give a short list of top players in different categories so you can match them to your needs.

What to consider when choosing a CTV agency
- Campaign goal: brand awareness, reach/frequency, direct response or full-funnel performance.  
- Inventory access: programmatic vs. direct buys on Roku/Hulu/AMAZON/streamers/publisher networks.  
- Targeting capabilities: audience data, household targeting, addressable TV, cross-device linking.  
- Measurement and attribution: brand-lift studies, incremental reach, sales lift, MMM or Causal Lift (VideoAmp, Samba TV, Nielsen, IAS).  
- Creative capabilities: 15/30/interactive / dynamic creative optimized for CTV.  
- Fraud and brand safety controls, and transparent reporting.  
- Budget and geography: some agencies specialize in US streaming; others are global.  
- Technology stack: DSPs, SSP partners and measurement vendors they work with.

Top options by type (widely used / well-regarded)
- Global media agencies (full-service, large-scale buys & strategy): GroupM (Mindshare, Wavemaker), Omnicom Media Group (OMD, PHD), Publicis (Zenith, Starcom), Dentsu (Carat, iProspect), IPG (UM, Initiative). Good for big-brand campaigns and premium inventory access.  
- Programmatic specialists / DSP-driven: The Trade Desk, Amobee, Simulmedia, Cadent. Good for highly targeted, performance-focused CTV buying.  
- Publisher/platform direct solutions: Roku OneView, Amazon Ads, Hulu/Disney/Peacock direct buys — useful when you want premium, platform-native placements.  
- Supply-side / streaming ad tech vendors: Magnite (SpotX), Xandr/Microsoft Advertising — important if you want strong supply relationships and programmatic access.  
- Measurement / analytics partners to expect or require: Nielsen (digital and CTV measurement), VideoAmp, Samba TV, Innovid, IAS.  
- Creative & personalization specialists: Innovid, Celtra, or integrated creative teams at the big holding companies for interactive or dynamic CTV creative.

Which is “best” for common scenarios
- Brand awareness and premium streaming placements: use a global media agency or direct buys with Roku/Hulu + measurement partner.  
- Performance / direct response with household-level optimization: The Trade Desk, Amobee or Simulmedia with strong measurement.  
- E-commerce / retail-focused: Amazon Ads (for Amazon properties) plus a programmatic partner for reach.  
- Small budgets or regional campaigns: boutique agencies or programmatic specialists that can run efficient, targeted buys.

Next step I recommend
- Tell me your primary goals (brand, performance, sales lift), budget range, geography and target audience. I’ll give a tailored short list (3–5) of agencies/platforms best suited to your needs and what to include in an RFP or test campaign.

If you want a quick starter: for broad, enterprise-grade CTV work consider GroupM (Mindshare/Wavemaker), The Trade Desk (programmatic DSP) and Roku OneView (direct-platform buys) — they cover most use cases between them.
